Sergio — thanks for the ping and forwarding the tracked file. Quick read and our recommended positions below. I've attached a clean-draft response (MSA_response_draft.pdf) with inline explanations.

1) Term / auto-extension (MSA §4.2) — position: we push back on removing auto-extension entirely. Proposed compromise: 36-month firm term with an option to extend up to 24 months via mutual written agreement, and a customer-initiated exit window tied to material SLA failures (three breaches in a rolling 12-month period). This preserves predictability for both sides.

2) SLA guardrails — propose explicit remedy schedule (service credits) before termination right vests. We should quantify service-credit percentages in Exhibit F and make termination contingent on not achieving cure within 60 days after the second breach.

3) Data residency — we can offer log archival to EU for >90 day retention as a paid add-on (covers storage/egress). Draft language in Exhibit D references encryption at rest and archival location. Need Product to confirm feasibility and estimate one-time migration cost.

4) Pricing hold — we can lock current rates for 24 months (rather than full 60) as a commercial concession in exchange for the 60-month commitment. Sales to confirm if that is acceptable.

Timeline: if we get Product's capacity confirmation today, Legal/Contracts can provide a marked counter and summary for the customer by end of day tomorrow (EOD 11/16).

Let me know if you want me to send directly to Aisha (I can attach the marked response and a one-page summary of positions).
